title: WKConversions × bFound
eyebrow: WKConversions × bFound · 39.5 s · 16:9 · voice-over, music, effects
headline: A great partnership creates more than great work.
subtitle: A SaaS-style partnership film in the Minimal Gradient SaaS look, built from both brands: WKConversions' blue glowing in from one side, bFound's indigo from the other. Two glass tiles linked by a cable carry the story: the film WKConversions made for bFound, the response it got on LinkedIn, the €1,000 that keeps most businesses out, the lock both partners open together, and the code BFOUND50 typed into the contact form as it is spoken: €400 becomes €200.
music_credit: Music: "Ramp It Up" by Ahjay Stelino, Mixkit (Mixkit Stock Music Free License), fitted to the film.

direction.Purpose: Announce the WKConversions × bFound offer: 50% off the €400 startup video with code BFOUND50, for LinkedIn and the two sites; it must read with the sound off.
direction.Audience: Founders and small businesses who follow bFound and WKConversions and have wanted a motion design video but found it out of reach.
direction.Format: 16:9, 1920×1080, 30 fps, 39.5 s. ElevenLabs voice (Christina, energetic commercial), force-aligned word by word (the code letter by letter); music and 76 effects mixed to −15 LUFS.
direction.Core message: Because the partnership worked so well, WKConversions and bFound make professional motion design accessible: code BFOUND50 on wkconversions.com/contact, €200 instead of €400.
direction.Look: Minimal Gradient SaaS: a near-white frame glowing into a mesh gradient (WKConversions blue, bFound indigo, lilac, bFound's cream), frosted-glass tiles and windows, thin cables with travelling pulses, Inter Tight 800 with the key phrase in the blue → indigo gradient, bFound's own logo and Instrument Serif for the ×.
direction.Motion: Flow: cables draw and carry pulses, tiles arrive with a soft scale-and-fade, content builds (keyframes, counts, typing). The stage floats in gentle 2.5D (a slow drift and tilt that never stops, a push per chapter); background chips and the dot grid travel at their own depths. Median frame motion 4%.
direction.Thread: The cable between the two tiles: it links them, carries the film to bFound, arches over the response, pulls the lock open with both tiles, feeds the code, and holds the end lockup.

beats.title: A great partnership
beats.caption: A great partnership creates more than great work.
beats.idea: WKConversions' tile slides in from the left, bFound's from the right, and a cable links them; on 'more than great work' the work itself (the film WKConversions made for bFound, its own frame) grows out of the link and rings go out from it.

frames.moves: Tiles slide in, the cable draws, a pulse travels.

frames.shows: The work grows out of the link.

beats.title: Made by WKConversions, for bFound
beats.caption: Made by WKConversions for bFound.
beats.idea: The window moves to the maker; a timeline appears and its playhead builds the film (b-mark, Found., the url pill) keyframe by keyframe; on 'for bFound' the finished film travels along the cable into bFound's tile, which takes a check.

frames.shows: The film being made on its timeline.

frames.moves: The film travels along the cable.

beats.title: The response
beats.caption: The response showed us how much impact the right video can make.
beats.idea: bFound's tile opens into the LinkedIn post by its founder, with the film in it; comments stream in (anonymous: gradient discs and skeleton lines, never a name or face), the reactions climb to 118 and the comments to 45, and the video comes forward and plays.

frames.moves: The post grows out of bFound's tile.
Counts climb, reactions float up, the video plays.

beats.title: €1,000 per video
beats.caption: Inaccessible to many businesses.
beats.idea: The typical price counts up to €1,000 / video; it rises over a professional motion design video; a glass wall locks it away; six small businesses reach for it and stop at the wall.

frames.moves: The price counts the whole phrase long.
The wall slides in, the lock clicks.
Their reach stops at the wall.

beats.title: WKConversions × bFound changed that
beats.caption: WKConversions × bFound changed that.
beats.idea: WKConversions' tile comes in, then bFound's; both cables pull on the lock until it opens, the wall falls, and every business connects to the video.

frames.moves: The wall falls, cables turn solid.

beats.title: Code BFOUND50
beats.caption: 50% off our startup price.
beats.idea: Both tiles feed the referral-code field; BFOUND50 is typed letter by letter exactly as it is spoken, and the field takes a check; −50% lands, then €400, the WKConversions startup price.

frames.moves: Each letter on its spoken letter.

beats.title: Claim it on wkconversions.com/contact
beats.caption: Claim your video for €200.
beats.idea: The contact page opens as the address types itself on the words; the form's referral code already holds BFOUND50; the cursor submits and €400 is struck through as €200 counts down into place.

frames.moves: The address types on the words.

beats.title: End card
beats.caption: Your video for €200 at wkconversions.com/contact
beats.idea: The two tiles come back together with the × between them, the code BFOUND50 and where to claim it; the cable keeps pulsing and the stage keeps floating.

open: The form on wkconversions.com/contact labels the field "Referal Code"; the film spells it "Referral code". Fix the form, or should the film match it?

Music: "Ramp It Up" (Mixkit) lands its drop on "So WKConversions and bFound…" but its final chord comes 0.8 s before the end card (an accent carries the card). Two fitted alternatives are kept in the session's scratch folder if you'd rather hear something warmer.
The LinkedIn counts (118 reactions, 45 comments) are as harvested on 6 Oct 2026; they will grow.
